summary.name: Cursor Voice
summary.one_liner: A native macOS voice assistant that lives next to your cursor, sees your screen, clicks and types for you, and answers out loud using your own OpenAI API key.
use_cases: automating repeated routines with saved macros
live web search with sources while working on a Mac
summary.what_it_does: Cursor Voice is a macOS app: press a hotkey or say "Hey Cursor" and a glowing orb appears next to the cursor. It takes screenshots on demand, reads the screen with Apple Vision OCR, and takes a fresh capture after each action to verify the result. It targets UI elements through the macOS Accessibility tree first, falls back to on-screen text, and uses simulated mouse input only as a last resort. It supports spoken conversation over the OpenAI Realtime API with interruption, saves durable local memory, can record and replay macros, and loads plugins defined as small JSON files.
notable: Native Swift app (about 3 MB), not Electron, MIT licensed and on GitHub
Targets UI via the Accessibility tree before falling back to OCR and mouse simulation
Bring your own OpenAI key with a live cost meter and credit budget; memory stored in a local file
Plugin marketplace and macro recording to replay routines
caveats: Requires your own OpenAI API key and pays OpenAI per use
Self-signed and not notarized, so first launch needs right-click Open
Requires macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon and Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions
Still in early versions (v0.8) and may occasionally miss clicks
